title: Matching fibrations of a right resolution detect mapping equivalences
statement: Use the model-category and homotopy-function-complex conventions of [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and the simplicial Reedy matching objects of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Let $Z$ be a fibrant object of a model category $\mathcal M$. There exists a Reedy fibrant simplicial object $Z_\bullet:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal M$ and an objectwise weak-equivalence coaugmentation $\operatorname{const}Z\to Z_\bullet$, with $Z_0=Z$ and degree-zero coaugmentation the identity. Any such choice has the following properties. For every $n\geq0$, its matching map $p_n:Z_n\to M_nZ_\bullet$ is an original fibration; here $M_n$ is the limit over proper face restrictions in the Reedy matching category, and $M_0Z_\bullet=1$. For every cofibrant $T$, the simplicial set $R(T,Z_\bullet)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(T,Z_n)$ is Kan and represents $\operatorname{Map}^h(T,Z)$, naturally in $T$. For every cofibration $u:U\to V$ with cofibrant source, the map $R(V,Z_\bullet)\to R(U,Z_\bullet)$ is a Kan fibration, and the following conditions are equivalent: (i) $\operatorname{Map}^h(V,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(U,Z)$ is an equivalence; (ii) $R(V,Z_\bullet)\to R(U,Z_\bullet)$ is a trivial Kan fibration; (iii) $u$ has the left lifting property against every $p_n$, $n\geq0$. A left lifting property means existence of a diagonal in every commutative square, as in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. Kan fibrations, trivial Kan fibrations and the boundary test have the meanings of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. No properness, combinatoriality or simplicial enrichment is assumed.

source.place: Hirschhorn, simplicial resolutions in Definition 16.1.2(2), the degree-zero-preserving simplicial-frame construction of Theorem 16.6.9 and the dual construction in Proposition 16.6.8(2), Theorem 16.5.2(2), Definition 17.2.1 and Theorem 17.8.4(4)-(5), Proposition 17.8.5(1), Proposition 17.8.8(4)-(5); for p:Z to the terminal object and the constant terminal resolution. Printed pp. 318, 331-332, 338-339, 350, 369-372. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: Choose the universe bound from [def-weil-size-convention] and regard $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ as the Reedy category for simplicial objects. Apply the relative Reedy extension/factorization statement of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] to the map $\operatorname{const}Z\to 1$ (the constant terminal diagram), fixing degree zero to be $\operatorname{const}Z_0=Z\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}Z_0$ followed by the fibrant map $Z\to1$. At degree $n>0$, after all smaller degrees have been fixed, factor the induced map $Z\amalg_{L_n\operatorname{const}Z}L_nZ_\bullet\to M_nZ_\bullet$ in the ground category $\mathcal M$ as a trivial cofibration followed by a fibration, and use the middle object as $Z_n$. The relative Reedy formulas then make the assembled arrows a Reedy trivial cofibration and a Reedy fibration, respectively. The resulting object $Z_\bullet$ is Reedy fibrant, the coaugmentation $\operatorname{const}Z\to Z_\bullet$ is objectwise a weak equivalence, and its degree-zero component is the identity.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Definition 16.1.2(2), printed p. 318, and Proposition 16.6.8(2) with Theorem 16.6.9 and its degree-zero-preserving construction, pp. 338-339. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text:
Because $Z_\bullet\to1$ is Reedy fibrant, the Reedy matching formula of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] identifies its degree-$n$ matching map with the original fibration
$p_n:Z_n\to M_nZ_\bullet$; for $n=0$ the matching category is empty, so $M_0Z_\bullet=1$ and $p_0$ is the fibrant map $Z\to1$. This proves the matching-map clause for every $n\ge0$.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Definitions 15.3.2-15.3.3, printed pp. 288-289: apply the relative matching formula to the terminal diagram. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text:
Now fix any resolution satisfying the statement, and let $T$ be cofibrant in $\mathcal M$. In the opposite model category $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}}$, the opposite of $Z_\bullet$ is a Reedy cofibrant cosimplicial frame on the cofibrant object $Z^{\mathrm{op}}$: the coaugmentation reverses to the frame augmentation and degree zero remains the identity. Apply the cosimplicial-frame mapping theorem [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping] in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}}$ with fibrant target $T^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its mapping simplicial set has $n$-simplices
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}}}(Z_n^{\mathrm{op}},T^{\mathrm{op}})=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(T,Z_n)$, hence is exactly $R(T,Z_\bullet)$. The theorem therefore makes $R(T,Z_\bullet)$ Kan and identifies it, naturally in $T$, with $\operatorname{Map}^h(T,Z)$. Here the Reedy latching object in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $(M_nZ_\bullet)^{\mathrm{op}}$, since its colimit is the opposite of the original matching limit; its latching map is $p_n^{\mathrm{op}}$, a cofibration by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. For the mapping-space identification, the universal property of localization in [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping] identifies $(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}})_\infty$ with $(\mathcal M_\infty)^{\mathrm{op}}$: taking opposites converts functors inverting $W^{\mathrm{op}}$ into functors inverting $W$. Reversing the two arguments therefore identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}})_\infty}(Z^{\mathrm{op}},T^{\mathrm{op}})$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M_\infty}(T,Z)$. Postcomposition by a morphism of the targets $T^{\mathrm{op}}$ corresponds degreewise to precomposition by the original morphism of sources $T$; hence this identification respects the induced restriction map.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Definition 17.2.1, printed p. 350, and Corollary 16.5.3(2), pp. 331-332; the cited cosimplicial-frame theorem supplies the identification with coherent localization, applied to the opposite model category. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: If $u:U\to V$ is a cofibration with cofibrant source, then $V$ is cofibrant by composition with the initial cofibration, using the composition closure of left lifting classes in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. In $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}}$, $u^{\mathrm{op}}:V^{\mathrm{op}}\to U^{\mathrm{op}}$ is consequently a fibration between fibrant objects. The fibration clause of [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], applied to the frame $Z_\bullet^{\mathrm{op}}$, says that postcomposition with $u^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a Kan fibration. Under the identification in the preceding step this is precisely $R(V,Z_\bullet)\to R(U,Z_\bullet)$.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Theorem 16.5.2(2) and Corollary 16.5.4(3), printed pp. 331-332; equivalently the fibration clause of the cited frame theorem in the opposite model category. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: The natural identification of Step 3 carries $R(V,Z_\bullet)\to R(U,Z_\bullet)$ to $\operatorname{Map}^h(V,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(U,Z)$. By Step 4 this map is a Kan fibration. In the Kan–Quillen model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], a Kan fibration is a trivial Kan fibration exactly when it is a weak homotopy equivalence. Thus condition (ii) is equivalent to condition (i).

source.place: Hirschhorn, Definition 17.2.1, printed p. 350, Theorem 17.8.4(4)-(5) and Proposition 17.8.5(1), pp. 369-370, specialized to the terminal map; the cited frame and Kan-Quillen statements give the direct argument. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: Fix $n\ge0$. A map $\partial\Delta^n\to R(V,Z_\bullet)$ specifies a map $V\to Z_k$ for every proper injective face $[k]\hookrightarrow[n]$, compatible with further face restrictions. Every simplex of the boundary factors uniquely as a degeneracy of such an injective face, so these compatible maps determine and are determined by the whole boundary map. By the universal property of the matching limit this is exactly a map $V\to M_nZ_\bullet$; a map $\Delta^n\to R(U,Z_\bullet)$ is the same as a map $U\to Z_n$. Under these identifications, a commutative square with the boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ and the map $R(V,Z_\bullet)\to R(U,Z_\bullet)$ is exactly a commutative square with left side $u$ and right side $p_n$. A diagonal in one square is exactly a diagonal in the other. For $n=0$, the boundary is empty and the same statement uses $M_0Z_\bullet=1$. Therefore $u$ has the left lifting property against every $p_n$ if and only if $R(V,Z_\bullet)\to R(U,Z_\bullet)$ has the right lifting property against every boundary inclusion. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], the latter is equivalent to being a trivial Kan fibration, proving (ii)$\Longleftrightarrow$(iii). The meaning of the left lifting property is the square-and-diagonal condition of [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure].

source.place: Hirschhorn, Lemmas 16.3.6(2)-16.3.7(2) and Proposition 16.3.8(2), printed pp. 324-325, and Proposition 17.8.8(4)-(5), pp. 371-372; face and degeneracy compatibility give the displayed square correspondence.
